blurb: From Jesus and Paul in Roman Judea through councils, empire, schism, and Reformation to a global faith of many churches.

events.description: Jesus of Nazareth preaches the kingdom of God in Roman Judea and is crucified under Pontius Pilate (c. 30 CE); his followers proclaim his resurrection.
events.title: Life & teaching of Jesus

events.description: Paul's letters to young churches around the Aegean — written a generation before the Gospels — are the New Testament's oldest layer and shape its theology of faith and grace.
events.title: Paul's letters — the earliest Christian writings

events.description: Mark (c. 70), then Matthew and Luke, then John arrange traditions about Jesus into narrative Gospels; Acts traces the movement's spread across the Roman world.
events.title: The Gospels composed

events.description: Summoned by Constantine, bishops define Christ as 'of one substance with the Father' against Arius — the creed later completed at Constantinople (381).
events.title: Council of Nicaea

events.description: The Edict of Milan (313) legalizes Christianity; by 380 the Edict of Thessalonica makes Nicene Christianity the Roman Empire's official religion.
events.title: From tolerated to state church

events.description: Writing after the sack of Rome in 410, Augustine contrasts the City of God with the earthly city — a framework for Western Christian thought for a millennium.
events.title: Augustine's City of God

events.description: Benedict of Nursia's Rule balances prayer, work, and study for monastic communities; Benedictine monasteries become engines of literacy, preservation, and mission in early medieval Europe.
events.title: Benedictine monasticism

events.description: Mutual excommunications between Rome and Constantinople in 1054 formalize the split between Western (Catholic) and Eastern (Orthodox) Christianity.
events.title: The Great Schism

events.description: Thomas Aquinas's unfinished Summa systematizes theology through Aristotelian reason — the summit of medieval scholasticism.
events.title: Aquinas & the Summa Theologiae

events.description: Luther's Ninety-Five Theses (1517), against the sale of indulgences, ignite a movement that splits Western Christianity; by 1555 Europe is formally divided between Catholic and Protestant states.
events.title: Luther & the Reformation

events.description: The Catholic Church's global council modernizes the liturgy (Mass in local languages), affirms religious liberty, and opens dialogue with other faiths.
events.title: Second Vatican Council

events.description: From the Azusa Street revival in Los Angeles (1906), Pentecostal and charismatic movements grow into the largest bloc of world Christianity, especially across Africa, Latin America, and Asia.
events.title: Pentecostalism & global Christianity

name: Christianity
